summary: Weekly POC sync focused on a new edge-case where short streaming sessions show TTFT spikes during microbursts. Discussed kernel choice tradeoffs, sequence-length routing, and quick mitigation (hedging + KV cache warm). Agreed on experiments and deliverables: kernel matrix, microburst re-run, and scheduling infra deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-09 11:00 PT / duration 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Samira (CSM), Priya (Vectra Eng Mgr), Carlos (SRE), Lina (ML Eng), Omar (PM), Jules (QA)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me?
[00:06] Priya: Yep loud and clear.
[00:08] Daniel: Good morning, afternoon folks, we'll jump into the microburst traces and then kernel decisions.
[00:14] Carlos: Quick note, we had another incident last night where TTFT spiked to about 420ms for like 30 requests, not the usual tail.
[00:24] Maya: Ok that's exactly what we want to triage today, thanks Carlos. Lina you got the latest logs?
[00:30] Lina: Yup uploaded to the drive, link in the chat, but quick note the test harness was using sequence length cap at 512 for the first run, then 128 for streaming.
[00:40] Omar: And timeline: customer wants pilot decision by Friday next week.

[01:02] Daniel: Alright jumping into the trace, at 00:00:23 of your microburst we see a sudden queue of concurrent streaming sessions, each with small prompts, that's causing kernel selection to flip to the dense kernel and the context switch cost is high.
[01:20] Priya: Sorry can you rephrase "dense kernel" — is that like our quantized path?
[01:24] Daniel: "Yeah poor word choice, so we have the 'fastpath' kernel for short sequences with small batch sizes and the 'matrix' kernel for longer sequences. During microbursts the scheduler sometimes mispredicts and picks matrix which is slower for first token.
[01:38] Carlos: I think our trace shows the scheduler chose the matrix one because of a rolling average of sequence length — the rolling window is 60s, which made it sticky.
[01:50] Daniel: Exactly, the window looks too wide, and the policy hedging isn't aggressive enough.

[02:12] Maya: So we have two quick fixes: reduce the seqlen window to 10-15s for routing decisions, and introduce immediate hedging to fastpath when observed concurrency spikes.
[02:24] Priya: Hedging meaning we send a duplicate request down fastpath? Concerned about cost.
[02:28] Daniel: Not duplicate full payload, more like speculative request for first token — we can cancel the slower path once fastpath returns. Cost is small relative to SLA hits.
[02:38] Jorge: [inaudible] sorry who's Jorge? (background voice)
[02:42] Jules: That's our QA environment voice.

[03:00] Lina: One more nuance — our prompts vary a lot, some are short clarifications, others are document summarizations, so seqlen distribution is tri-modal. That confuses the routing.
[03:16] Maya: Good point. Daniel any ideas for per-route pinning?
[03:20] Daniel: We can do model-route pinning by endpoint label, so low-latency endpoints get fastpath with a quota. For mixed endpoints we can enable a probabilistic hedging threshold.

[03:46] Carlos: Also security question: if we enable short hedging, will logs or KV cache leak across paths? We're on VPC with HSM, but concerned about cross-tenant cache warm.
[03:58] Samira: We recommend per-tenant KV namespaces; the hedged request uses same tenant namespace so no cross-tenant exposure. We'll send the design note.

[04:20] Priya: Ok, let's look at numbers. Last week's baseline TTFT p50 was 45ms, p95 180ms, but during microbursts p95 jumped to 420ms and p99 to 1.2s.
[04:36] Daniel: Yes those p99s align with kernel flips + cold KV. We also saw GPU context switch overhead on certain kernels.

[05:10] Maya: Do we have a quick mitigation you can roll out today?
[05:14] Daniel: Short term: reduce routing aggregation window to 10s, enable speculative fastpath hedging at 10% for endpoints flagged as low-latency; also pre-warm KV cache for recurring user prefixes. That should knock p95 down by 30-50% in the microburst scenario.
[05:34] Priya: How confident on that estimate?
[05:36] Daniel: Medium confidence; based on replayed traces with synthetic hedging we saw p95 drop from ~420ms to ~240ms.

[06:02] Omar: Any downside?
[06:04] Daniel: Cost bump from speculative calls and slightly more KV ops; plus potential increased GPU occupancy if many hedges fire.

[06:20] Carlos: For Dedicated pilot we're ok with modest cost increase if it meets SLA. Our team is more worried about variability than average cost.

[06:40] Lina: One weird artifact — on node GPU-3 we saw much worse TTFT than GPU-1 for same workload. Could be kernel build or driver mismatch.
[06:52] Daniel: Good catch, we'll run a kernel parity check across the fleet and check driver versions. Could be an AVX path fallback too.

[07:10] Priya: Another question — sequence length routing: can we pin certain user cohorts to seqlen-optimized instances?
[07:18] Maya: Yes that's a feature we sketched in the console — per-route affinity and reserved lanes. We'll share UI screenshots.

[07:34] Jules: From QA perspective, if we pin we'll need a canary for correctness and hallucination regression tests.
[07:44] Samira: We'll coordinate evals and provide a prompt set for regression checks.

[08:02] Daniel: Quick note on kernel selection matrix: for attention pattern 'local' and seqlen <=64, fastpath wins p50/p95. For seqlen>256 the matrix kernel is better. For mixed patterns the hybrid kernel might be best but it's sensitive to batch size.
[08:26] Priya: Could you put those thresholds in a spreadsheet?
[08:28] Daniel: Yep Daniel -> will attach a matrix after the call.

[09:00] Carlos: Regarding observability, when kernel flips occur can we tag spans and emit a gauge for kernel-switch frequency?
[09:08] Daniel: Yes, we can add an event and expose it in the console. We'll add a dashboard tile and an alert when switch rate > X per minute.

[09:36] Maya: Onto experiments: the team proposed three runs — (1) seqlen-window shrink + hedging, (2) kernel parity and driver checks, (3) pre-warm KV and prefix caching. Priya does that align?
[09:52] Priya: Yes. We'll run (1) and (3) in staging, (2) needs infra window.

[10:10] Lina: For pre-warm, how do we populate the KV cache? We have user history but privacy says we can't store all tokens.
[10:18] Daniel: We can store derived prefixes or hashed context keys; it's tenant-scoped and encrypted at rest via your KMS. Samira will share the KMS integration note.

[10:38] Omar: Any compliance red flags?
[10:40] Samira: None immediate — per-tenant namespace and KMS usage keeps us inside SOC2 policy; we'll share the compliance excerpt.

[11:00] Priya: On timeline: we'll run microburst replays today, send logs, and expect Redwood kernel matrix by Friday. Then we meet Wed for infra deep dive.

[11:18] Maya: Perfect. Lina, can you confirm the microburst run parameters?
[11:22] Lina: We'll run 5 bursts, each 100 concurrent streams, seqlen distribution [8, 64, 512], with 30s spacing. Upload by EOD.

[11:34] Daniel: If you can also tag which sessions are from the 'clarify' route vs 'summarize' route that helps pinning tests.

[11:44] Priya: Will do. One more question — do you recommend Dedicated or Hosted for this workload?
[11:50] Maya: For now Dedicated gives predictable latency but Hosted with routing policies and reserved lanes could work. We'll include cost/latency tradeoff in the pricing note.

[12:06] Carlos: For the parity check: Daniel, can you run a quick gpu_util and driver compare script?
[12:12] Daniel: I'll run parity and return a short report by tomorrow morning.

[12:22] Jules: QA will also run long-run stability overnight once microburst configs uploaded.

[12:36] Samira: I'll share the hedging design doc and per-tenant KV notes.

[12:50] Maya: Recap: Daniel -> kernel matrix and parity check; Samira -> design/compliance notes; Maya -> pricing & Dedicated options; Priya/Lina -> run microburst and upload logs; all to reconvene Wed 2027-06-16 for infra deep dive.

[13:12] Priya: Sounds good, thanks all.
[13:18] Omar: Appreciate it, bye.
[13:20] Maya: Thanks everyone, end call.

Note: timestamps in transcript are approximate; the live transcript had occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, "matrix kernel" sometimes transcribed "matrix turbine").
